title: iPscDB: a comprehensive platform for plant single-cell transcriptomic data integration and analysis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad record. Requested the homepage and three guessed download paths with the fetch helper and with curl using a browser user agent: every request returned HTTP 403, with a Chinese web-firewall page saying the request was blocked as a security threat.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about content comes from the abstract alone: 4,688,428 cells, 288,139 curated markers, 946 experiments, 38 plant species, uniform reprocessing, automated cell-type annotation benchmarking, and a Marker Confidence Level scheme. No download format, file size or licence was visible.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: the iPscDB site returns HTTP 403 (blocked by a web firewall) for every URL tried, with no mirror in Zenodo, Figshare or GEO linked to the DOI. Data can't be obtained from here.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked (no files). The likely label, cell type per cell, comes from author or automated annotation that would have to be harmonised across 946 experiments and 38 species, so it would effectively be constructed.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked; expression matrices presumably exist on the site but could not be reached.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked; no file or documentation reachable.

a5_enough_rows.note: Paper only: 4.69M cells and 946 experiments are claimed; not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; the full atlas of 4.69M cells is likely tens of GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Estimate only; a single-species subset could fit, but nothing could be downloaded to check.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Could not compare: no download or API reachable.

a8_label_provenance.note: Paper only: cell-type labels are cluster annotations, partly from the platform's automated annotation, which is itself a model output (circular). Markers are partly 'database-derived associations' computed from the expression data, so they leak from the features.

existing_models.name: scPlantLLM (transformer foundation model for plant single-cell data, GPB 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported up to 0.90-0.91 zero-shot annotation accuracy on independent Arabidopsis datasets, with transfer to maize and rice (from search snippet).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved beyond the abstract snippet.

existing_models.name: scPlantFormer (lightweight plant single-cell foundation model, Research Square preprint)
existing_models.score_and_split: Claims 92% cross-species annotation accuracy; pretrained on 1M Arabidopsis cells (snippet).

existing_models.name: scPlantAnnotate (transformer cell-type annotator, J. Advanced Research 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Beats other methods in Arabidopsis, maize, rice and soybean under random-split evaluation (snippet).

backbone.name: scPlantLLM (plant single-cell transformer)
backbone.hardware: CPU possible for a small subset; GPU preferred

honest_claim_h3: Not reachable: with no downloadable data, the model could only claim to reproduce cell-type labels that were themselves produced by annotation pipelines.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-cell gene expression from many plant species to predict each cell's type, including in species not seen during training.
plain_idea.train_on: Gene-expression profiles of individual plant cells from 946 experiments in 38 species (4.69 million cells claimed; not verified).
plain_idea.predict: The cell type of each cell, taken from the authors' cluster annotations, partly produced by automated tools rather than an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Plant biologists working on crops with few single-cell studies could label new datasets without hand-curating marker genes.

more_or_better_data.why: 38 species and 4.69M cells (paper claim) is broader than scPlantLLM's and scPlantFormer's mostly-Arabidopsis pretraining of about 1M cells, but none of it could be downloaded.

confidence_score.why: The labels are annotations with no replicate measurement, so nothing supports calibrated confidence beyond what the existing classifiers already output.

models_beatable.why: The 2025-26 transformer models report about 0.90 accuracy, often on random splits; a cross-species held-out test could expose weaknesses, but they aren't old or weak.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The data is not accessible, and labels come from different labs' annotation schemes, so the 'same quantity measured the same way' condition fails.

ml_idea: Cross-species plant cell-type annotation, with the held-out species as the split. Dead because the data can't be downloaded and the labels are annotation outputs.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Open https://www.tobaccodb.org/ipscdb/homePage from a normal browser (maybe outside a blocked region) and confirm that a bulk download of the expression matrices plus cell-type labels exists; this failed here with HTTP 403.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: the only data host (tobaccodb.org) blocks every request with HTTP 403, and there is no repository mirror, supplement or open full text. Even if reachable, the cell-type labels are annotation-pipeline outputs (A8 risk), and three plant single-cell annotation models (scPlantLLM, scPlantFormer, scPlantAnnotate) already exist.
